As a youth, he reclaimed his father's magical crane-skin bag and held a spear against his forehead to resist the sleep-inducing harp of Aillen. His two dogs refused  to kill a deer that this man married after she regained her form as a woman named Sadb. This father of Oisin [oh-SHEEN] will awake from his slumber at the hour of greatest need, and he gained wisdom by burning his thumb as he cooked the Salmon of Knowledge. Name this woodland warrior from Irish mythology.

An assassination attempt against this person failed when he did not take the plane named the Kashmir  Princess to the Bandung Conference, where he stated "The population of Asia will never forget that the first atom bomb exploded on Asian soil." Unlike He Long, this leader took the Little Long March,  ending up in Hong Kong shortly after the Nanchang Uprising. A dispute over when to stop mourning the death of this person led to the Tiananmen Incident, which almost prevented the rise of Deng Xiaoping, and which allowed supporters of this person to continue opposing the Gang of Four. Name this first Foreign Minister of the People's Republic of China, who for many years served under Mao Zedong as China's Premier.

This person was John Nance Garner's spokesman during Garner's first presidential campaign and  negotiated the selection of Garner as vice president. He chaired the Interstate and Foreign Commerce Committee when it passed the Emergency Railroad Transportation and Federal Communications  Acts, and he brought money home to his district by supporting the Red River project. When Joseph Byrns died, this person became House Majority Leader, and when William Bankhead died in 1940, this person became Speaker of the House. Identify this Texan who is the namesake of a congressional office building and who was the longest serving House speaker in United States history.

The night before this battle, an enemy gun battery fired upon the USS McCulloch when its smokestacks  accidentally flared up. This battle ended after the USS Baltimore destroyed a gun battery at Sangley Point in order to expose a fort at Cavite [kah-VEE-tay]. This battle began as the Asiatic Squadron,  led by the USS Olympia, opened fire on Admiral Montojo's fleet, once Captain Gridley was told he "may fire when you are ready". Name this opening battle of the Spanish- American War in which Commodore Dewey decisively defeated a fleet near the Philippine capital.

This group settled in Pannonia after being defeated by King Geberic. That movement took place  under the leadership of Wisimar, who belonged to the Hasdingi tribe. After Hilderic was replaced as leader of this group by Gelimer, this group was defeated by the Byzantines under the leadership  of Belisarius. This group moved to Africa, and soon after that they conquered Sicily, Sardinia, and Corsica. Just after Roman emperor Valentinian III died in 455, this group, under the leadership of Genseric, sacked Rome. Name this Germanic tribe whose name has become synonymous with someone who defaces property.

This leader was prompted by the deaths of his earls Edwin and Morcar at the Battle of Fulford  to march north, where, according to folklore, a giant axeman held up his entire army. Afterwards, this leader fended off an invasion led in part by his brother Tostig. At a later battle, this leader's  housecarls led a charge down Senlac Hill, where this leader apocryphally died by an arrow to his eye. Name this English king who defeated the forces of Harald Hardrada at the Battle of Stamford Bridge, only to be killed weeks later at the Battle of Hastings by the forces of William the Conqueror.

When this person was the UK prime minister, he helped establish King's College London and  successfully pushed for passage of the Catholic Relief Act. Those successes were achieved about a year before the death of George IV. Much earlier, this person served as governor of Seringapatam and  defeated the Maratha Confederacy at the Battle of Assaye. He was the only man to have held the positions of Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief of his countries army at the same time. Allying with Gebhard von Blücher, name this politician and general, who was victorious over Napoleon Bonaparte at the Battle of Waterloo.

This person was loved by Marshal Danville, who unwittingly took the poet Chatelard to see her,  but Chatelard was found hiding in her bedroom. When this person was seven months pregnant, her husband became convinced that her secretary had impregnated her, so his friends murdered that  secretary, David Rizzio. This queen was believed to have written sonnets and eight letters to the Earl of Bothwell, which supposedly implicated this person in the death of Lord Darnley, her husband. This daughter-in-law of Catherine de Medici was executed for her role in the Babington Plot. Her son becoming James the Sixth, and he later became James the First of England. Name this queen executed for attempting to overthrow her cousin Elizabeth the First.

One side in this war isolated and encircled enemy forces into pockets called motti  at the Battle of Raate Road, and then stopped the enemy's advance towards the city of Oulo at the Battle of Suomussalmi. After Semyon  Timoshenko took command of the invading side in this war, it breached the Mannerheim Line. Simo Hayha recorded 505 sniper kills and was nicknamed the "White Death" in this war that introduced the term "Molotov cocktail". This three-month-long conflict resulted in the Soviet Union being expelled from the League of Nations and gaining territory near Leningrad. Name this offensive against Finland during World War II that took place during its namesake season.

This organization, which in 1971 controlled the ship Phyllis Cormack, is trying to stop the production  of golden rice. One of its supporters, Peter Willcox, is part of a group being charged with piracy and hooliganism. That group, which calls itself the Arctic 30, tried to get from their ship Arctic Sunrise  to an oil rig, and they have been held in Murmansk since September by Russia. This group started out as the Don't Make a Wave Committee. Willcox, an American, once captained this organization's Rainbow Warrior. Name this opponent of nuclear power that takes part in environmental activism.

Thomas Jefferson wrote a letter to William Short saying that they belonged to this school of philosophy,  which received some support in the Renaissance starting with Lorenzo Valla. In Oenoanda, which is in modern-day Turkey, its tenets were carved onto a large stone wall. One of its followers, who  used the term clinamen to describe the unexplainable swerving of atoms, was Lucretius. Believers of this philosophy tried to attain ataraxia by denying the existence of an afterlife. Identify this ancient Greek school that met in The Garden and which is often contrasted with Stoicism.

Section 301 in this law was invoked when Benjamin Owens was not given arbitration in an attempt  to save his job in what became the Supreme Court case Vaca v. Sipes. The president objected to its controls on some newspapers and its use of anti-Communist oaths. This law furthered the Sherman  Antitrust Act's ban on secondary boycotts, and that ban was strengthened twelve years after this law was passed by its successor, the Landrum-Griffin Act. Passed over the veto of Harry Truman and named for a New Jersey congressman and Ohio senator, this bill revised the Wagner Act. Name this act that outlawed closed shops, passed in 1947 in reaction to a series of strikes.

This group established a colony at Fort Caroline in Florida, but they were later killed by the Spanish. This group was protected by Francis I until the Affair of the Placards, when Francis' bedchamber door was covered with an anti-Catholic poster. The rights of this religious group were officially revoked in 1685 by the Edict of Fontainebleu, which overturned Henri IV's Edict of Nantes. Name this group of French Protestants who were massacred at the St. Bartholomew's Day Massacre.

In one incident in this colony, members of the Aquascogoc tribe were accused of stealing a silver cup, causing Sit Richard Grenville and his men to burn their village. One of this colony's governors, John White, was the grandfather of Virginia Dare, the first English child born in the Americas. Upon White's return to this colony, he found "Croatoan" carved on a tree, but all of the colonists missing. Name this "lost colony" founded by Sir Walter Raleigh in the Outer Banks of North Carolina.

This man started his campaign against the Portuguese by attacking their hold on West India at the Siege of Diu. This leader also instituted many legal reforms, including raising the rayas from serf status, earning this man the moniker "the Lawgiver." This sultan was able to gain a foothold in Hungary in 1526 after defeating Louis II at the Battle of Mohacs. Identify this sultan who succeeded his father, Selim I, and ruled during the "golden age" of the Ottoman Empire.

One author from this nation wrote about the disappearance of Ambrose Bierce during this country's civil war and wrote about a corrupt soldier on his deathbed who reflects on his sinful life in The Death of Artemio Cruz. This country is the home of the author of the poem "Sunstone" and the essay collection The Labyrinth of Solitude. One author from this country wrote about Esperanza's experiences in The House on Mango Street. Name this home country of Carlos Fuentes, Octavio Paz and Sandra Cisneros.

During this conflict, the Battle of Ramillies was won by the Duke of Marlborough. Tallard was defeated by Eugene of Savoy at the Battle of Blenheim during this war. Louis XIV refused to remove his grandson during negotiations to end this conflict. The Habsburg Charles II appointed a Bourbon as heir to the throne, which sparked this conflict because of the competing claim of Charles of Austria. Name this war that was ended by the Peace of Utrecht after which Philip V became king of a certain Iberian nation.

One member of this family built the Palais du Luxembourg while acting as regent for her son, Louis XIII. In addition to that member, Marie, this was also the family Pope Clement VII, who refused to annul Henry VIII's marriage. Two members of this family were attacked during Mass at the Duomo as part of the Pazzi ["paat-zee"] conspiracy to remove this family from power. Although this family held significant political power, they initially gained power through banking. Name this powerful family of Florence, whose members include Cosimo and Lorenzo the Magnificent.

Early in this man's career, he was responsible for convincing Virginia to relinquish the land that would become the Northwest Territory. As Secretary of State, this man failed to deliver the commissions for the "midnight judges," resulting in this man being sued by William Marbury. This man was also helped write a number of essays to promote the Constitution with John Jay and Alexander Hamilton known as the Federalist Papers. Name this "Father of the Constitution" and fourth president of the United States.

The institution defined by this document passed a law that called for the division of land north of the Ohio and east of the Mississippi river to be divided into predefined sizes and sold with a tax. The pitfalls of this document were highlighted when there was no centralized response to a Massachusetts rebellion. This document was created by the Second Continental Congress, which had earlier drafted the Declaration of Independence. Name this first plan for government in the United States of America, which was replaced by the Constitution.
Articles of Confederation and Perpetual Union

This leader built a temple near Luxor that bears his name and contains the House of Life, an extensive library filled with works about this man. A statue of this ruler and his daughter Bentaneth appears at the Karnak temple, which he built along with his father Seti I. To commemorate his supposed victory over Muwatallis and his army of Hittites at Kadesh, this man built the twin Abu Simbel temples, and he built a massive tomb for his favorite consort, Nefertari. Name this Egyptian New Kingdom pharaoh who is called "the Great."

This president created a Panel on Mental Retardation and passed legislation for mental health care. Martin Luther King was released from jail after the Atlanta protests by this president who forced the integration of Ole Miss. After the Bay of Pigs campaign attempted to overthrow Fidel Castro, this president ordered a blockade around Cuba to prevent the Soviet Union from building nuclear weapons there. Name this president who was assassinated by Lee Harvey Oswald in Dallas and was succeeded by Lyndon B. Johnson.

During this war, Lord Raglan defeated Menshikov at the battles of Inkerman and Alma. The Black Sea fleet won the naval battle at Sinope during this conflict. Gorchkov, one of this war's commanders, invaded the Danubian provinces of Moldavia and Wallachia. Military medical care became more sanitary during this war under the direction of Florence Nightingale. The Battle of Balaclava and the Siege of Sebastopol took place during this war. Name this war fought between the Russians and the Allied French and British over religious territory in the Ottoman empire.

This leader called for citizens to "avenge the dead" after his general Francisco de Miranda had surrendered. This leader's Panamanian congress failed. He was opposed by Jose Tomas Boves, whose group of llaneros was known as the "Legion of Hell." This author of the Cartegena ["carta-hena"] Manifesto met with Jose de San Martin at Guayaquil ["gua-ya-keel"], inspiring him to win the battle of Ayacucho. This man was victorious at both Carabobo and Boyaca, where he surprised Spanish troops by crossing the Andes Mountains. Name this "Liberator" of South America.

This leader crushed revolts led by Vercingetorix at the fortress of Alesia during his conquest of Gaul. This figure was appalled when pirates who had kidnapped him ransomed him for only twenty talents. During a civil war he started, this figure defeated Pompey, with whom he had formed the First Triumverate. This figure was stabbed in the Senate by his former allies, including Brutus, on the Ides of March. Name this Roman general who changed the Roman Republic into the Roman Empire.

One leader of this country refused to follow the traditional political practice of "café com liete" by not choosing his successor from the southernmost state. That leader, Washington Luis, was succeeded by Getulio Vargas, who established the "Estado Novo" in this country. The invasion of this country's Mato Grosso state by Francisco Solano Lopez's army began the War of the Triple Alliance, in which this modern day country formed an alliance with Argentina and Uruguay. Name this South American country whose first ruler was the Portuguese Dom Pedro I.

In this battle, a gunshot answered a call for surrender that was followed by a red flag symbolizing bloodshed. The misinformed General Sesma marched towards Colonel Fannin's army in Goliad instead of to this battle's site. Captain John W. Smith's reinforcements were slaughtered by the attacker who used ladders to scale the walls of the namesake fort. Defenders of the namesake fort refused to retreat from Santa Anna's forces during this battle in which both Jim Bowie and Davy Crockett were killed. Name this battle in San Antonio at the namesake Texas mission.

During this dynasty, rebel leader Li Zicheng attacked Beijing, and military commanders requested help from the tribesmen who remained after the rebels were forced out and founded the succeeding dynasty. This dynasty was founded when the Mongols were defeated during the Red Turban Rebellion. Its first emperor was the Hongwu emperor and its Yong-le emperor built the Forbidden City when the capital was moved from Nanjing to Beijing. Name this dynasty that ruled China between the Yuan and Qing dynasties that is known for its blue and white porcelain.

This event was headed by Boniface of Montferrat, and Baldwin was made the ruler of the political entity that formed as a result of this conflict. Pope Innocent III excommunicated all the participants in this event after the Siege of Zara, which was conducted with assistance from Enerico Dondolo, the doge of Venice. This crusade* resulted in the creation of the Latin Empire, with the crusaders choosing to capture a different city instead of attacking Jerusalem. Identify this crusade that ended with the sacking of Constantinople.

One of these acts includes a khutba sermon, is prepared for by tahara, and concludes with the taslim, which is uttered to angels perched on participants' shoulders. During one of these acts, participants run seven times between Safa and Marwa before the final tawaf. These acts include zakat, voluntary almsgiving, and sawm, purification and fasting. The first of these duties is a declaration of faith, shahada. Adherents make a pilgrimage to Mecca known as the hajj, one of these acts. Name this set of five acts considered essential by Muslims.

This man served under Winfield Scott and led troops in the Battle of Chapultepec [cha-pul-ta-peck] during the Mexican-American War. This leader was defeated in all of the Seven Days Battles, but defeated Joseph E. Johnston at Seven Pines. He removed McClellan from the gates of Richmond, and fought McClellan again at Antietam, all while leading the Army of Northern Virginia. This general won at Fredericksburg and Chancellorsville, but was forced to surrender at Appomattox. Name this general in charge of the Confederate Army during the Civil War.

Oscar Wilde is buried in this city's Pere Lachaise Cemetery. Its business district is known as La Defense, and Montparnasse Tower is found in this city near the Lafayette Shopping Center. The Chatelet Theatre is located in this city, whose museums include Pompidou and the Orsay. Sacre Coeur stands atop this city's hill of Montmartre. This city's Fauborg St. Antoine is home to the Bastille, while the Seine River runs through this city. Name this French city which features such landmarks as Notre Dame Cathedral and the Eiffel Tower.

One king of this name passed the Reform Bill that eliminated rotten boroughs and was the brother and successor of George IV. Another king of this name was invited by the Immortal Seven to overthrow James II in the Glorious Revolution. One king of this name compiled the Domesday Book and defeated Harold Godwinson for the Crown of England at a battle depicted in the Bayeux Tapestry. Identify this name shared by a king from Orange who ruled jointly with Mary, and a Norman conqueror who won the Battle of Hastings.

This ruler removed King Cotys from his thrown and annexed the Bosporan Kingdom. During his reign, the general Corbulo made peace with Parthia, but this emperor requested Corbulo's suicide anyways. He fell out of his chariot at the Olympic games, but won anyways. After she protested his affair with Poppaea, this emperor had his mother Agrippina the Younger bludgeoned to death. His reign saw the Great Fire of Rome, and he killed himself before he could be beaten to death by the Senate. Name this emperor who reportedly fiddled while Rome burned.

This man's mother became a nun after he was taken by Niniane, and he became a monk after the death of his king. This son of King Ban and Helen made his home at the Joyous Guard. This subject of the Vulgate Cycle allowed the jester Daguenet to capture him and he befriended Galehaut, who delivered messages to his lover. This figure was seduced by Elaine, with whom he fathered the hero of the Quest for the Holy Grail, Galahad. This knight rescued his lover from Maleagant. Name this knight who was raised by the Lady of the Lake and had an affair with King Arthur's Lady Guinevere.

One movement in the 1960s saw this province's government create a welfare state and take over education and health care from the Catholic Church. After that movement, known as the Quiet Revolution, James Cross and Pierre LaPorte were kidnapped here, which prompted the only peacetime enactment of the War Measures Act by Pierre Trudeau to quell the October Crisis. Those kidnappings were perpetrated by the FLQ in an attempt to further their agenda of independence for this province. Identify this primarily French- speaking Canadian province with capital at Montreal.

Pope Hadrian II appealed to this leader for help defeating the Lombard Desiderius, after which this man conquered Pavia and took over the Lombard crown. This leader advanced to Saragossa, but when Ibn al-Arabi's forces failed to appear to confront Cordova, this man retreated, losing to the Basques at Roncesvalles. This ruler was the son of the first king of the Carolingian dynasty, Pepin the Short, and co-ruled with his brother for a time before Carloman died. Name this king of the Franks and emperor of the Romans.

This country was claimed by Ruy Lopez de Villalobos after natives of this country killed Ferdinand Magellan. Manuel Roxas was the first president of this independent nation, while Manuel Quezon was the first president of this country's Commonwealth. Emilio Aguinaldo led a guerrilla war against the US in this future nation. One dictator from this country had his rival Benigno Aquino Jr. Assassinated. This nation's capital was liberated from the Japanese by Douglas MacArthur. Name this island nation once ruled by Ferdinand Marcos, with capital at Manila.

Operation Glimmer distracted defenders before this battle, causing them to believe that the fighting would be at Pas de Calais. The weather convinced defenders no attack was imminent, with one commander leaving to celebrate his wife's birthday. Operation Tonga was the codename for British paratroopers who landed and attacked the Merville Artillery Battery in this battle. Other forces in this battle landed at Pointe du Hoc, Sword, Juno, and Gold beaches. Name this World War II battle in which Allied Forces attacked German-occuped France after American troops landed at Omaha and Utah beaches.

This leader headed the Senate War Investigating Committee during World War II. He developed a 21-point program addressing Social Security, employment, and public housing that became known as the Fair Deal. This leader created a program to aid Greece when it was threatened by Turkey. His presidency saw an economic recovery plan for western Europe, the Marshall Plan. This president negotiated to create NATO and ordered troops to defend South Korea. He ordered the bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki, after which Japan surrendered. Name this president who took over after FDR died.

This leader was given the Appomattox surrender table for his critical role in the surrender of Robert E. Lee while he led a division under Philip Sheridan. This officer defeated Black Kettle's band, and later led troops to meet with those of John Gibbon and George Crook, who was defeated by Crazy Horse at Rosebud Creek. This leader of the 7th Cavalry arrived at a village before Gibbon's troops, split his men into three divisions, and attacked the village, but was forced to retreat to a ridge and was defeated and killed by Lakota warriors. Name this officer whose ‘Last Stand' was at the Battle of Little Bighorn.
